title: Compress PDF
about: Compress PDF uses local PDF structure optimization to rewrite object streams and remove avoidable serialization overhead where possible. It preserves the document pages and embedded content. This browser-only implementation does not render pages or downsample embedded photographs, so image-heavy PDFs may not become smaller.
steps: Choose one valid PDF file up to 25 MB.
Start PDF optimization. The document is read and re-saved locally using compressed PDF object streams.
Review the reported size comparison. If the rewritten file would be larger, the original is retained instead.
Download the optimized PDF and open it in a PDF reader to confirm that its pages and content remain intact.
capabilities: Local pdf-lib structural reserialization with object streams. This can reduce some PDF structural overhead but does not recompress embedded images, rasterize pages, remove fonts or guarantee a smaller result. The original is retained when optimization would increase file size. Password-protected PDFs may not be supported.
benefits: This workflow can make a repetitive image or file-size optimization task more approachable by keeping the relevant action in one place. It may be useful when preparing images for websites, forms, documents, presentations, archives, or everyday sharing, depending on the selected operation. Working from a copy is recommended whenever the original file is important. A quick review of the output helps catch quality changes, unsupported content, or formatting differences before the file is used elsewhere.
limitations: Supported input types are the formats listed in the workspace. Browser processing can be affected by device memory, browser version, image dimensions, and file complexity. The required processing integration is not configured as a verified working service in this project; the page must not imply that processing has completed. Conversion and compression can change quality, metadata, transparency, color handling, or layout. Always verify the exported file in its intended destination. faqs.question: How do I get the best result?
faqs.answer: Start with a clear, correctly oriented source file and review the available settings before processing. Inspect the actual output rather than relying only on the preview or filename.

faqs.question: Will the result always match the original quality?
faqs.answer: Not necessarily. Editing, conversion, resizing, and compression can affect detail, color, transparency, metadata, or layout. Keep an untouched copy of important source files.
